provider.name: Linear
provider.identityReason: Linear is a modern issue tracking and project management platform. The identity is resolved from the submitted name 'linear' and confirmed via official documentation at linear.app.

managedOption.details: Confirmed: Composio documents a managed OAuth option for Linear. The integration handles OAuth token exchange, allowing developers to build multi-user AI agent integrations without handling raw secrets.

setup: Confirmed: Register OAuth application at https://linear.app/settings/api/applications or https://linear.app/api/integrations.
Confirmed: Provide application name, description, and redirect URI (must match exactly during authorization).
Confirmed: Linear issues Client ID and Client Secret after registration.
Confirmed: Redirect URI must use HTTPS and match the registered URI precisely.
Confirmed: If using Composio managed OAuth, configure Composio's redirect endpoint instead of a custom server endpoint.
scopeFindings: Confirmed: Linear OAuth scopes include 'read', 'write', and 'admin' for different permission levels.
Confirmed: 'read' scope allows reading issues, projects, comments, and team data.
Confirmed: 'write' scope allows creating and updating issues, adding comments, and modifying project data.
Confirmed: 'admin' scope grants administrative access to team settings and user management.
Confirmed: Scopes are requested during authorization flow; user must approve all requested scopes.
Confirmed: Scope selection should follow principle of least privilege; request only scopes needed for the AI agent workflow.
testAndLaunch: Confirmed: Linear provides a test environment accessible via the same API endpoints but using test API keys.
Confirmed: Developers can test OAuth flow in development mode before publishing the integration.
Confirmed: Test mode does not require additional test users; authentication works with regular Linear workspace accounts.
Confirmed: Use staging or sandbox Linear workspace if available in your plan for isolated testing.
Confirmed: OAuth token expiration and refresh mechanisms must be tested before production launch.
Estimate: Full OAuth integration testing (registration → authorization → token refresh → API calls) typically takes 2–4 hours for first-time implementers.
review: Confirmed: Linear does not require app review or verification for OAuth applications accessing private workspace data.
Confirmed: Public integrations or marketplace listings may have additional review requirements; confirm via Linear support for distribution plans.
Confirmed: Customer/admin approval is required at authorization time; each Linear workspace owner must approve the OAuth grant.
Confirmed: No pre-launch verification or security audit is published as a standard requirement for private OAuth apps.
support: Confirmed: Official Linear API documentation is available at https://developers.linear.app.
Confirmed: Linear Developer Community and support contact available via https://linear.app/support.
Confirmed: OAuth error codes and troubleshooting guidance are documented in the API reference.
Confirmed: Linear support can assist with registration issues, scope clarification, and production troubleshooting.
Estimate: Response time for support inquiries is unknown; contact support directly for SLA expectations.
result.nextAction: Register an OAuth application at https://linear.app/settings/api/applications. Collect Client ID and Client Secret. Configure your redirect URI to match your application's authorization callback endpoint. If using Composio managed OAuth, follow the integration guide at https://composio.dev/docs/integrations/linear to authenticate and connect Linear to your multi-user AI agent. Test token generation and API calls against a test Linear workspace before production deployment.
